Afraid of it? Man, no. Heck no. If anything, I'd pay good money to gain some weight right about now. Like I was just saying with that old belt and my jeans... I want to actually fill out my clothes again, you know? I look in the mirror sometimes, like right after I get out of the shower, and I just see these ribs poking out all sharp, and my collarbones looking like they're trying to punch right through my skin, and it just looks plain awful. Why in the world would I be scared of putting some meat back on my bones? I ain't trying to be no underwear model or nothing. I'm just a regular guy who wants to look regular again. 

If I woke up tomorrow and stepped on the scale and saw I put on ten pounds, or even if I just had a little bit of a gut starting to show, I'd probably throw a damn party. I really would. I'd go down to the store and buy something to celebrate, even if I couldn't stomach eating it. It's just... the whole idea of being scared of getting fat when you're practically blowing away in the wind, it just don't make a lick of sense to me. 

I used to be a pretty sturdy guy, you know? Not heavy, but solid. Like I could hold my own. Now I'm just... I don't know, frail. I hate that word, especially for a guy my age, but that's what it is. Frail. I bump into a doorframe and it feels like I'm gonna bruise down to the bone. So no, doc, I ain't scared of gaining weight one bit. I'm practically praying for it, honestly, I just can't get the food down to make it happen.

Yeah... yeah, I really have. And it's a crying shame, honestly, because I didn't used to be this way. I used to have things that kept me busy, you know? Like, I used to love going for walks down by the lake. Just taking my time, walking along the water, watching the ducks or the folks fishing, just breathing in the fresh air. It gave me something to do with my hands since I ain't working.

I look at it, and I look at the ones I finished sitting up on the shelf, and I swear to you, doc, it's like they belong to somebody else. 

Like some other guy sat there and built 'em, and I'm just sitting in his house looking at his stuff. I just stare at them and I don't feel a single itch to pick up the glue or finish painting the engine block. It's just pieces of plastic to me now. I don't get no joy out of it, no spark, nothing. I just sit in my chair and look at the box, and I can't for the life of me remember why I ever cared about putting it together in the first place. It's like the part of my brain that actually liked doing things just dried up and blew away, leaving me with nothing to do but just sit there.

I don't... I don't think so, doc. I really don't. Because, see, it ain't just about being tired or feeling weak. Like I was saying just a minute ago about the lake and those little model kits... it's a whole lot deeper than just not having the juice in my batteries, you know?

Like I said, I look at that '68 Mustang sitting there on the card table in the living room, and it really does feel like it belongs to somebody else entirely. If I had all the energy in the world, I'd still just be staring at a stranger's pieces of plastic. The part of me that actually got a kick out of it, the part that cared if the silver paint on the engine block was perfectly even or if the ducks at the lake were getting enough bread... that part is just gone. 

It's like somebody came in while I was sleeping and snipped the wire that connects me to the things I used to like. I can see the models, I can remember that I used to like them, but I can't *feel* it. So, sure, if I had more energy, maybe I'd be standing up instead of sitting in my chair when I look at 'em, or maybe I'd pace around the room, but I'd still be looking at 'em like they ain't mine. I just don't have it in me to care about 'em anymore, energy or no energy. It's just a totally dead feeling.

It's just... it's really messed up my body, being this skinny all of a sudden, and I just don't know how to get my stomach working right again.\n\nDoctor: Have you been trying to lose weight?\n\nPatient: No, no, Lord no. I ain't trying to go on no diet or nothing like that. I mean, why would I be doing that on purpose? I ain't got no job to look fancy for, I ain't trying to be on TV or impress nobody. It's just... I don't know, it's like my stomach just flat out shut off. \n\nYou know how when you're sick with a bug or something, and the very thought of, like, a heavy meal just makes your guts turn over? It's like that, but every single day. I'll go into the kitchen and open the fridge, right? And I'll just stand there with the door open, feeling that cold air, and I'll look at the cheese, or the lunch meat I bought Lord knows how long ago—it's probably gone bad by now anyway—and I just feel... tired. Just looking at it makes me tired. The chewing, the swallowing, figuring out what to put on a plate... it all just feels like way too much work for a guy who's just sitting at home anyway. \n\nSo no, I ain't trying to lose a single pound. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well... see, that's the thing, doc. Like I was just saying a minute ago about how they feel like they belong to some other guy... it ain't just about getting the engine running, so to speak. It's not just that I can't get out of the chair. Because, truth be told, I have tried. I really have.

I've picked up the little plastic pieces, held the little tube of glue in my hand, and tried to make myself just... I don't know, just glue the bumper on. Just one piece, I told myself. But even sitting right there, actually trying to do it, holding the things in my own two hands... nothing. There's just no spark. I'm just a guy holding a piece of plastic. I don't care if it gets glued on straight or crooked or if it gets glued on at all. It's exactly like I said, I look at my own hands doing it and it feels like somebody else's hobby. 

And the lake, too... say somebody drove me down there and pushed me out the car door right onto the walking path. I'd just be standing there looking at the water, and I wouldn't care about the ducks or the folks fishing or the fresh air. I wouldn't enjoy it one bit. It's not that I just can't get started, it's that the part of me that actually liked doing those things... it's just completely gone. Like I told you, I used to really like walking by the lake and working on my little model kits, I really did, but now... now they just sit there, and even if I force myself to touch 'em, I just look at them like they belong to somebody else entirely. Doing it doesn't bring the feeling back. The feeling is just dead.

I ain't trying to go on no diet or nothing like that. I mean, why would I be doing that on purpose? I ain't got no job to look fancy for, I ain't trying to be on TV or impress nobody. It's just... I don't know, it's like my stomach just flat out shut off. \n\nYou know how when you're sick with a bug or something, and the very thought of, like, a heavy meal just makes your guts turn over? And I'll just stand there with the door open, feeling that cold air, and I'll look at the cheese, or the lunch meat I bought Lord knows how long ago—it's probably gone bad by now anyway—and I just feel... tired. Just looking at it makes me tired. The chewing, the swallowing, figuring out what to put on a plate... it all just feels like way too much work for a guy who's just sitting at home anyway. \n\nSo no, I ain't trying to lose a single pound. If anything, I wish I could just sit down and eat a normal plate of food like I used to, maybe a big bowl of chili or something, but my body just says nope. It's real frustrating, you know? Because people see you getting all bony and they probably think you're doing it on purpose, but I'm just sitting there staring at a piece of bread wishing I actually wanted to eat the damn thing.\n\nDoctor: Are you ever afraid of gaining weight?\n\nPatient: Afraid of it? Man, no. Heck no. If anything, I'd pay good money to gain some weight right about now. Like I was just saying with that old belt and my jeans... I want to actually fill out my clothes again, you know? Well, let's see... it's been a while now. This whole thing, this heavy, gray cloud just sitting right on top of me... it's been hanging over me for about five months now.

Well, doc... it's kind of hard to pull those two things apart, you know? The sad thoughts, the guilt, the emptiness... they're always there, playing on a loop. Sleep... man, sleep is just a whole other mess. You'd think, since I'm so tired, like I was just saying about the wet sand and all, that I'd just close my eyes and be out like a light. But it ain't like that. Not at all.

I just lay there waiting for the morning, which I don't even want to come anyway since I got nothing to do but sit in my chair. 

And the real kicker is, doc... even when I do sleep, even when I get a few hours in between all that staring at the wall and waking up in the dark, I don't feel rested at all. Not one bit. I wake up and I feel completely worn out, like I spent the whole night digging ditches instead of laying on a mattress. It's just exhausting. Pleasure? No... no, doc, not even for a second. Not even a tiny little spark. 

I mean, I try, you know? Sometimes I'll get up from the chair and I'll walk over to that little folding table I was telling you about, just to see. Just to test it out, I guess. And I used to like walking by the lake, too, just being out there in the air. But now... now they just sit there. The model kit just sits on the table collecting dust, and the lake is just... out there, and I don't care about either of them. 

And the really crazy part, the thing that really messes with my head when I stand there holding that little plastic car part, is that I look at it... and I look at them like they belong to somebody else. Like some other guy bought that paint. Like some stranger set up that table in my room and I'm just looking at his stuff. It doesn't feel like mine anymore. It's like the guy who enjoyed those things just packed up and left, and I'm just the empty shell he left behind in the room. So I just put the piece back down on the cardboard box, exactly where I found it, and I go right back to my chair. Because what's the point? There's just no joy in it. Not even for a split second. It's all just dead to me now.
